Commentary.Commentary: Three days, three one-sided games. Australia have stomped to the top of the table and in all likelihood, Pakistan will join them at the top and take them through to Sunday's final with two games to spare in between. Don't agree? Well we hope you are right. Alistair Campbell feels that a blockbuster game is in store for us on America's Independence Day when Zimbabwe take on Pakistan in Game 4 of the tri-series at 1000 local (0800 GMT). Wish that we get what he has promised. We are signing off for now but the real blockbuster is coming up in a few hours' time - England take on India in the first T20I in Manchester. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

VICTORIOUS CAPTAIN AARON FINCH IS THE MAN OF THE MATCH FOR HIS... record. He does not smile though - puts in a stern look and says that it is nice to get the award. Then looks at the team's fielding and bowling and bluntly says that Australia were shoddy and the Zimbabwean batsmen took full toll. Agrees that he was trying to look at all his bowling options in the stack. Is happy with the bowling of Andrew Tye and Ashton Agar in the middle overs. Finally manages a smile when asked whether he enjoyed his innings - says that you get such moments only once or twice in your lifetime and he certainly enjoyed it.

Zimbabwean skipper, Hamilton Masakadza manages a smile. Says that just when he thought it could not get any tougher after the first game, it did. Admits that Zimbabwe could not do anything right from the time Finch unleashed himself. Looking back at the two games, Hamilton feels that too many runs are being given post the Powerplay. Finds some positives in the openers today and hopes that someone puts their hand up tomorrow against Pakistan.

Nice net session for the Aussie bowlers. They were in for some stick early on, raising false hopes of a fascinating run chase but were barely tested other than Solomon Mire. Barring D'Arcy Short, who was unlucky not to get a wicket, thanks to a dropped catch from Andrew Tye, every other Aussie bowler who bowled got a wicket. Agar choked the runs upfront with 2/16 in 4 overs while Tye tied up the tail-enders with a 3-fer. Aaron Finch did a pretty decent job of rotating his bowlers giving everyone a go, barring himself. The presentation coming up...

As expected, after the Aaron Finch onslaught, nothing much came from the Zimbabwean batsmen, except the initial burst from Solomon Mire. They raced to 50 in the 5th over but once he got out, well, the cookie just crumbled. You know you are in trouble if Chisoro comes in at number 8, which is so long a tail.

BIGGEST VICTORY MARGIN FOR AUSTRALIA in T20Is in terms of runs - beating their previous best of 95 against South Africa at the 'Gabba in 2006. Courtesy this win, they now have one foot of the size of Billy Stanlake in the final.
ZIMBABWE DO NOT GET BOWLED OUT. A good achievement, given the procession that started post Mire's dismissal. A yorker around off, Nyumbu digs it out towards cover. AUSTRALIA WIN BY 100 RUNS!
A huge cheer from the crowd as Muzarabani plays a lovely-looking drive towards long on for one.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards fine leg for a run.
FOUR! Nice shot, sir! Outside off, short in length, John upper cuts it over backward point for a boundary!
Outside off, Nyumbu walks across, then tries to run it down to third man and jog but gets a bottom edge past his stumps towards the keeper.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
One over to go for Stumps...
Full and around off, watchfully blocked.
On middle and off, whipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, John looks to flick but misses.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Outside off, Nyumbu looks to cut but misses.
John Nyumbu walks in, no, strides in at number 11, doing some jig to the music being played by the DJ. Flashes a big smile to his partner.

OUT! 6th Aussie to get a wicket today. A short ball, outside off, Mpofu goes for the pull but is done in by the extra bounce. Gets a top edge which goes straight up in the air. Stoinis thinks about going to his right but then D'Arcy Short runs in from short mid-wicket to complete the formalities.
On the cards perhaps but not on the scoresheet. Tye himself 'SPOILS' the over by bowling a full toss outside off and CM works it through mid-wicket for a single. Tye's figures read 3-1-6-3!
Outside off, Chris looks to run this down to third man but is beaten on the inside. Another wicket maiden on the cards?
Full and outside off, Mpofu backs away and drives this straight to short extra cover.
Excellent yorker on middle, pushed to the off side.
Full and down the leg side, flicked straight to short fine leg.
Blessing Muzarabani walks in at number 10. Zimbabwe have 17 balls left...
OUT! Caught at long on. Third wicket for Tye. Rolls his knuckles over, bowls it on a length on middle and leg, Burl is early into his slog and can only find Jhye Richardson at long on.
Andrew Tye is back on. 2-1-5-2 so far.
Outside off, Chris looks to open the face of his bat and run this down to third man but is beaten on the inside. 10 from the ageless over.
Down the leg side, Ryan tickles it towards fine leg for a run. For those interested, 109 more are needed from 19 balls.
ANOTHER WIDE. This is turning out to be a never-ending over in a never-ending match. A slower bouncer attempted, but it is outside leg and well above the batsman.
WIDE. Another extra ball. Down the leg side, flick shot missed.
Nice footwork. Walks well across his stumps even before Marcus can let the ball go. It is outside off and Mpofu works it through mid-wicket and gets a single.
On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
WIDE. Extra ball, down the leg side, Ryan misses his tuck.
FOUR! A length ball down the leg side, Burl gently tickles it to the fine leg fence.
Marcus Stoinis is given an opportunity as well.
This time he stays in his crease and drives it towards long off for a single. Good finish from Jhye - he was 1/18 in 2 overs - has gone for just 5 in his last 2.
A short ball outside off, Burl comes down the track and looks to swat but misses.
Walks across his stumps and flicks it towards fine leg for a single.
Full and straight, watchfully blocked.
Down the leg side, tucked towards fine leg for a single. A run has been scored after 8 dots on the trot...
On middle and off, pushed to the off side.
Jhye Richardson to bowl out - 3-0-20-1 so far.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. A maiden for Agar to finish his spell - 4-1-16-2.
Lunges to play the sweep but misses and is hit yards outside off. Still, Carey appeals for LBW. Not given.
Full and outside off, watchfully blocked out again.
Comes down the track but can only defend it back to the bowler.
Outside off, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Chris Mpofu walks in at number 9, replacing Chisoro.
OUT! Gone this time. On middle and leg, Tendai swipes across the line but it has gone only as far as a 10-meter jog needed by Agar to complete the catch from the mid-wicket boundary.
SIX! WHAM! Even Maxwell smiles looking at that. A short ball outside off, Chisoro backs away and heaves it over long on!
Now he attempts the reverse sweep, only to glove it to short third man.
Outside off, played towards point.
Full and outside off, Chisoro looks to sweep but misses and the ball goes off his pads to short third man.
A short ball to start, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
Glenn Maxwell time. Finch testing out his options on possibly who all could bowl.
Slow yorker ball on middle, nicely dug out. A WICKET MAIDEN FOR TYE - 2-1-5-2 so far.
On middle and leg, watchfully pushed to the leg side.

Darren Bravo walks in to bat. Oops sorry. Looking at the image on the television screen, it seemed like Little Bravo has walked out to bat. Been watching too much of cricket. Just last night, saw him celebrate a catch on a Free Hit in the Global T20 Canada League... anyways the new man in is Tendai Chisoro.

OUT! Chigumbura's struggle ends. The knuckle ball from Tye, ties up Elton who looks to swing this out of the park. Himself has to get off the park now. The ball has not even carried to long on because the fielder has taken it well inside the ropes. Second wicket for Tye in 6 balls.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
On middle and leg, pushed towards mid on but the bowler himself rushes to his right to stop it.
Outside off, on a length, Chigumbura pushes it towards point. Wants a single but is sent back.
Full and wide outside off, Ryan looks to drive but misses. The ball barely carries to the keeper who is not able to stop it cleanly.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh pad.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.

100 IS UP FOR ZIMBABWE. Not bad considering one looks at the overs bowled. But then, they had reached 52 in the 5th over. The second phase has been slow. On leg stump, Burl looks to work it to the leg side but misses due to the slowness of the delivery. Gets a leading edge which flies to third man. Only a single.
Around middle and off, watchfully defended.
A short ball outside off, coming in, Chigumbura is months early into his pull and misses the ball. It hits him on the back and rolls towards third man. A leg bye taken.
Jhye Richardson is back on. 2-0-18-1 so far.
Outside off, pushed towards cover. 5 runs and a wicket from the over, 10/2 in the last 2 overs.
Ryan Burl walks in at number 7...

OUT! Soft dismissal. Andrew Tye gets himself in the scoring sheet for the Aussie bowlers. Full and outside off, Mire looks to push this down the ground but only ends up chipping it back to the bowler. Too easy a catch to be put down and Tye ensures that he hangs on. Zimbabwe would have wanted more from Moor. 42/0 becomes 98/5.
Outside off, punched towards mid off. That almost got through beneath the bat.
Hits the deck hard, gets extra bounce, Moor hops and works it towards short mid-wicket.
On middle, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Billy Stanlake drops back to the third man boundary now...
FOUR! Nicely done! A short ball outside off, Chigumbura waits for the ball to come to him and guides it over short third man for a boundary!
Andrew Tye is going to bowl now...

Outside off, driven through the covers. D'Arcy Short runs all the way from sweeper cover to his right only to allow the ball through. But there is long off to mop it up. Two runs taken. 5 runs and a wicket from the over, in next to no time, Agar has bowled 3 overs with figures of 2/16.
Slowly tossed up outside off, pushed through the covers for one.
Full and straight, driven back to the bowler.
Elton Chigumbura walks in now. Some entertainment in store...
OUT! STUMPED! Saw him coming, did Agar and threw it wide outside off. Masakadza had nowhere to go after wandering out of his crease to defend and missed it. Easy stumping for Carey behind.
Drives this inside out to cover for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed through mid off for a single.
SIX! Aha... he has not thrown that up and Moor has thrown that back. Short and outside off, Peter goes back and pulls it way over long on! 16 from the over, Short's figures read 2-0-20-0!
FOUR! WHAM! Short goes full now and Moor gets down and slogs it over mid on, beating Andrew Tye at long on to his left! 'C'mon D'Arcs, throw it up, throw it up!' shouts Carey.
FOUR! Very well played. A long, long hop, on middle, Moor goes back and pulls it over square leg for a boundary!
Unfurls the reverse sweep but the length is a bit short, As a result, he gloves it over the keeper to short third man. A run taken.
A full toss, on middle again, swept graciously towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up on middle, watchfully defended.
Off the mark first ball, with a flick towards square leg for a single. 5 runs and a wicket from the over, Agar's figures read 2-0-11-1.
Who is next to join the procession? Peter Moor, the Zimbabwean wicket-keeper.
OUT! PLUMB LBW! Full and straight, Musakanda gets down low to sweep and often when you attempt that shot, you cannot miss. He misses and is adjudged LBW. Losing wickets in a bit of a cluster now...
Punches this down to long off and gets another single.
Full and outside off, driven down to long off for one.
Outside off, Masakadza goes inside out and lofts it over cover for a run.

Darts this down the leg side, Musakanda looks to flick and misses. The ball goes off his pads towards short fine leg and the batsmen take a single. No signal from the umpire, so must have been an inside edge.
Ashton Agar is back on.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single. Not a bad start from Short...
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh pad.
DROPPED! SIXTH ONE OF THE DAY. A short ball on middle, Hamilton goes back and heaves this towards long on. Andrew Tye comes in, misjudges it, dives forward but puts it down. A run taken.
Nicely bowled, good loop and flight, on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Another long hop, pulled away again for a run.
Short from Short, Masakadza pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
D'Arcy Short to try and bowl some left-arm Shane Warne spin...

SIX! Off the mark in grand style! A length ball outside off, Musakanda clobbers it over wide long on! 11 runs and a wicket from that over. Poor Billy - 4/8 yesterday and 3-0-39-1 already so far today. Welcome to cricket... Zimbabwe end their Powerplay on 63/2 as opposed to Australia's 75. Very good...
One-match old Tarisai Musakanda walks in at number 4, replacing Mire. Did well on debut against Pakistan a couple of days back.

OUT! Mire's innings ends. Plays one shot too many but you cannot blame him. The target is so steep that you need more than one boundary in an over, especially with the fielding restrictions on. Looks to heave this over mid on but cannot clear the fielder. Catching practice for Marcus Stoinis. It was good while it lasted - 28 from 19 from Mire, who hammered 5 fours and a six. Did not run much, eh...
Good thinking. Bowls it much fuller, outside off, SM pushes and misses.

Typical fast bowler's response. On the helmet. A short ball outside off, Solomon goes for the pull but is beaten for pace, rather than by it. The ball comes after he has played the shot and hits him on the grille. Seems okay.
FOUR! Smart shot! A short ball outside off, Mire deliberately upper cuts it, past the keeper to the third man fence!
Outside off, steep bounce, Masakadza looks to punch it through the off side but gets an inside edge down the leg side. A single taken.
Billy Stanlake changes ends...
FOUR! WHACK! Full and in the slot, Mire creates room and slogs it over mid on! 50 UP FOR ZIMBABWE IN 5 OVERS! 178 more needed in 90 balls...
On middle and off, watchfully blocked.
The batsman dances down the track but decides to defend it. One run added to the total.
On middle, pushed to the bowler.

Massive appeal for LBW but the umpire denies. Full and outside off, Solomon attempts a reverse sweep but misses and is hit right in front. Agar is so confident that it is out that he almost starts to walk towards his skipper to celebrate but then sees the umpire moving away on the LBW appeal! The ball has gone over the keeper to short fine leg and a single is taken. The umpire felt there was an inside edge - replays do not detect any. SM is lucky to get away with one...
Full and outside off, Mire looks to defend but is squared up and gets an inside edge.
Finch turns to spin. Ashton Agar introduced in the Powerplay.
FOUR! WALLOP! A short ball, outside off, this time Masakadza stays back and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary! A wicket from the over but 16 from it as well! 34 have come in the last 2 overs.
Much fuller now, outside off, watchfully defended.
That is a snorter now. A short ball to welcome the skipper, Masakadza comes forward to defend but is taken aback by the bounce. Fends it to the off side.
Skipper Hamilton Masakadza walks in at number 3, replacing Chibhabha.

OUT! Caught behind! That is a beauty of a delivery from Richardson and he has got a wicket. He lands this on a length outside off and Chibhabha's initial step is to try and run this down to third man. But the ball comes back in a long way and literally cramps the batsman for room. It takes the inside edge, hits the pad and then lobs to the keeper who appeals. Chibhabha starts to walk any which ways, before the umpire can raise his finger. So Finch's plans - of talking to his bowler before this ball and removing himself from slip - have worked wonders.
WIDE. Sprays this down the leg side, CC looks to tuck but misses. Australia under pressure. Finch walks all the way from slip to have a chat with his bowler...
SIX! Well played sir! Jhye drops it short and Chibhabha swivels and pulls it massively over square leg! 189 more needed from 100 balls now! The stand is worth 41 from just 20 balls...
WIDE. A short ball down the leg side, Chamu leaves it alone.

FOUR! Nicely played! On a length outside off, Chibhabha gives himself some room to the leg side and punches it through the covers. Splits the gap and finds the boundary! 196 more needed from 102 balls. Chibhabha moves to 12 from 8 balls. Nice to see the batsmen showing some intent.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery. 18 from the over and Stanlake's figures read 2-0-28-0!
FOUR! Sensible cricket from Solomon now. The ball is a decent one, on a length outside off, coming in, the batsman just waits for it and steers it past first slip to the third man fence!
SIX! Ho ho ho! The best of the over! A short ball outside off, Mire leaps and upper cuts it over point. The ball goes all the way!
FOUR! Edgy this time. A length ball outside off, Mire swings hard and gets a thick leading edge. Andrew Tye rushes to his left from third man but cannot get there!

FOUR! VIOLENCE! The hosts need more of these. Just the first boundary in the third over. Not all that short from Stanlake, Mire plays more of a short-arm jab than pull and clubs it over mid on for a boundary!
Nicely bowled. Hits the deck hard, bangs it in short, Mire taps it towards point.
On a length on middle and leg, turned through mid-wicket for a run. Decent start from Richardson.
On a length around off, defended solidly off the back foot.

An appeal for an LBW turned down! Fullish ball, angling in sharply, Mire falls over a bit in order to flick it but is hit on the pads. Australia appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Sliding down leg perhaps.
Sensible from Mire! In the same zone, the batsman lets it go.
That's a peach! Richardson lands this one in the avenue of apprehension and gets it to move away. Mire fishes at it and gets foxed.
Shortish ball well outside off, Chamu cuts it towards point where the fielder dives to his right and makes a half stop. Can't stop the single though.
Jhye Richardson to share the new ball from the other end.

Straying on the pads this time, Chibhabha tucks it nicely through the vacant square leg region. Some aggressive running between the wickets allows the batsmen to take the third run. 10 from the first over.
Good shot but for no run! Fullish ball outside off, driven crisply to the man at extra cover.
Wide! Short ball but the line is wayward again. It is down leg and Chamu ducks under it.
Hangs back to the shortish ball and punches it out.
Wide! Down the leg side, Chibhabha tries to whip it but misses.
Fullish ball on middle, kept out watchfully.

Shoddy stuff from the Aussies! Similar length ball, placed towards third man as the batsmen take a run. The fielder again scores a direct hit, this time at the striker's end but the batsman is in. Another run results.

Back of a length outside off, Chamu places it towards point and sets off. D'Arcy Short has a shy at the bowler's end and hits the stumps but the ball ricochets through mid-wicket. An extra run results.
Wide! A loosener to start off with! It is way outside off as Chibhabha has a flash at it but misses.
The players are back on! Billy Stanlake to start off proceedings. Solomon Mire and Chamu Chibhabha are the openers.
